title: Top 5 California Cities for Heat Pump Rebates (2026)
desc: A corrected 2026 ranking of California heat pump rebates by utility: Los Angeles, Glendale, Sacramento, Burbank and Riverside, with a 3-ton example for each and sources.
h1: Top 5 California Cities for Heat Pump Rebates (2026)
lead: An earlier version of this post said Los Angeles pays a flat $2,500 per ton and that a 4-ton system nets $10,000. That is not how LADWP pays now, and the state and federal money it counted has ended or is full. This version ranks what each utility actually publishes, read on October 2, 2026.
sections: The ranking, by a 3-ton gas-to-electric swap

The same 3-ton system earns very different amounts depending on the utility. Here is what each pays, from its own page.

Utility (city)What it pays3-ton, gas to electric
LADWP (Los Angeles)$1,000 to $1,250 per ton ducted, $1,500 to $2,500 per ton mini-split, by efficiency tier$3,000 ducted at the entry tier, $4,500 mini-split, up to $7,500
Glendale Water and Power$1,000 per ton, up to $5,000, replacing gas$3,000
SMUD (Sacramento)$3,000 variable-stage, $2,000 two-stage, replacing gas$3,000 (variable-stage)
Burbank Water and Power$1,000 per ton, up to $2,500 (up to $5,000 low-income)$2,500 (the cap)
Riverside Public Utilities$750 per ton, 15.2 SEER or higher$2,250
San Jose Clean Energy$1,500 flat ($2,500 in Environmental Justice communities)$1,500
Pasadena Water and Power$170 per ton, plus $20 per ton if bought in Pasadena$510

These are utility rebates only. Funding is limited, and every one of these programs can change.
Why Los Angeles still comes first

LADWP's top mini-split tier pays $2,500 per ton, so a 3-ton unit at 20.5 SEER2 and 9.1 HSPF2 earns up to $7,500. Most homes will land lower, because the entry tier for a ducted system is $1,000 per ton. LADWP's scale also rewards buying a more efficient model, which no other utility here does. See Los Angeles heat pump rebates.
Where Glendale, Sacramento, Burbank and Riverside land

Glendale's $1,000 per ton is simple and reaches $5,000 at 5 tons, but the water heater rebate of $4,000 is the bigger draw (Glendale). SMUD pays $3,000 for a variable-stage unit and also publishes what its customers paid, a median of $18,804 for a gas-to-electric heat pump (Sacramento). Burbank caps its standard rebate at $2,500 so a 3-ton system gets the same as a 2.5-ton one (Burbank). Riverside's $750 per ton is the highest flat per-ton rate (Riverside).
Big California areas with no utility cash rebate

PG&E (Fresno, Bakersfield, Oakland, Berkeley, Fremont), SDG&E and San Diego Community Power (San Diego, Chula Vista, Escondido) and Southern California Edison (San Bernardino, Ontario, Long Beach) have no open utility cash rebate for a heat pump that we could confirm. San Francisco pays up to $1,200 in bill credits over two years. Free upgrades for income-qualified households are available through several of them. The federal 25C credit ended after December 31, 2025, and TECH Clean California and HEEHRA are fully reserved for single-family homes.
faq: Which California city has the best heat pump rebate?
For a typical 3-ton system, Los Angeles (LADWP) at $3,000 to $7,500, Glendale at $3,000 and Sacramento (SMUD) at $3,000.
Does the rebate depend on the unit's efficiency?
At LADWP, yes: the per-ton amount rises with the SEER2 and HSPF2 tier. At most others it is a flat per-ton or flat amount.
Is there a statewide California heat pump rebate?
Not open for single-family homes. TECH Clean California and HEEHRA are fully reserved.
